input.summary: Both findings are fixed. First, every assertion that the branch current sensor reaches the controller over a path separate from or distinct from the isolated local bus is gone, in all four places it appeared. The detailed description now says only that the edge controller 100 is further coupled to the branch current sensor 104 of FIG. 1, over which coupling the sensor reports the measured branch current to the controller. FIG-1.md now says a line runs from the branch current sensor 104 downward and to the left, clear of the three rectangles, to the top edge of the edge controller 100 and joins the two, with no statement about the bus. The Brief Description of FIG. 3 now reads "the coupling of the edge controller to the branch current sensor". The supported plain coupling at the FIG. 1 paragraph of the description is untouched, and no geometry changed. Second, numeral 104 now designates the same part on every sheet. The FIG. 3 brief no longer puts 104 on a connection line while stating the sensor is absent: the sheet now shows a short horizontal line that is the branch conductor 102 above the controller outline, a small open rectangle straddling it that is the branch current sensor 104 shown schematically, and a line from that sensor down to the top side of the controller outline joining the two. The leader for 104 ends well inside that small open rectangle and the leader for 102 ends on that line away from any junction, so both leaders land on the bodies the numeral table names. I added 102 to the FIG. 3 numeral list in ascending order, giving that sheet 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 132, 134 and 136, which is eight numerals and within the per-sheet limit. draft/numerals.md, the claims, and the abstract are unchanged, and no part, numeral definition, or supporting text was removed. Re-verified after editing: all 23 numerals remain used in the description; each figure's geometry numerals match its own list exactly (FIG. 1 carries eight, FIG. 2 seven, FIG. 3 eight, FIG. 4 eight); the union still covers all 23; the briefs run 2515, 2621, 2767 and 2604 characters, all within the limit; and no placeholder, note, question, citation marker, or em dash appears in draft/ or figures/. Per the drafting brief, prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and the art available here may be incomplete.
reasoning: The separateness wording carried real technical substance, a second independent signal path, so removing it was the right call rather than trying to justify it. What the disclosure supports is that the branch current sensor is an independent safety input, which is a statement about the sensor's role in the protection process, and the draft already relies on that correctly where it says the sensor governs a protection process acting on the power path. Nothing in the claims depended on the wiring topology, so deleting it cost no scope.

Keeping the coupling itself was necessary: claim 1 recites a controller coupled to the branch current sensor and configured to act on a measured branch current from it, so the description has to state that the sensor reports its measurement to the controller. Only the qualifiers about how that connection relates to the bus came out.

For the numeral conflict I put the sensor on the sheet rather than dropping 104 from FIG. 3. Dropping it would have left the line entering the controller from above unidentified again, which was the earlier objection; drawing the sensor resolves both at once and adds no unsupported structure, since the branch current sensor and its coupling to the controller are both disclosed.

Adding the branch conductor 102 to FIG. 3 follows from showing the sensor: the disclosure has the sensor measuring total current on the branch, so it has to straddle something, and that something is the conductor already numbered in FIG. 1. Using the same numeral keeps one part to one numeral across sheets instead of inventing a new numeral for the same conductor.

I checked the sheet count before adding 102 and FIG. 3 now carries exactly eight numerals, the maximum, so no focused sheet was needed. I also trimmed one redundant clause in the same bullet to keep the brief clear of the length limit without removing any body, contact, or path the renderer needs.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is no document to cite or design around and no citation appears anywhere in the draft. The Background states the technical problems in the inventor's own terms: control-pilot signalling is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that responds slowly, coarsely, or not at all leaves the branch over its limit undetected by any scheme working from commanded values; the varying non-charging portion of the branch load either overcommits the branch or forces a permanently conservative configured limit; equal or request-proportional sharing perpetuates inequality between sessions that were served unequally; and welded contacts, an intermittent site link, and a hand-wired identifier-to-channel map each defeat allocation while leaving every component apparently functional. The independent claims recite the combination that answers those problems: per-connector verification of each pilot-assigned limit against the connector current sensor, together with an upstream branch current sensor whose persistent over-limit reading through a verification interval, after a reduced pilot command, triggers one-at-a-time contactor opening in a stored shedding order. That protection function rests on the sensor's disclosed role as an independent safety input, not on any wiring topology, which is why removing the separateness statements leaves the claimed combination intact. The dependent ladder retreats to the three-condition reclose permissive, then welded-contactor recording with same-branch inhibition and a local fault indicator, then offline operation under a signed local token and the last accepted branch limit with the branch-current protection still governing and tamper-evident meter records, then the sensor-confirmed installation mapping. Per the drafting brief the art supplied here may be incomplete, and this strategy should be revisited against any search results the attorney obtains.
